# TextStats project brief

## Purpose and audience

TextStats is a small Python utility for developers and command-line users who need predictable line and word counts for UTF-8 text. It will expose a silent importable API and a module-entry CLI with explicit output and failure contracts. This repository currently contains preparation documents only; functionality has not been implemented.

## Established requirements

The product request establishes Python 3.11+, the standard library and unittest. The public `textstats` module must directly export immutable `TextStats(lines: int, words: int)` with nonnegative values, `count_text(text: str, *, strip_bom: bool = True)` and `count_file(path: str | os.PathLike[str], *, strip_bom: bool = True)`. The CLI entry is `python -m textstats`.

Line counting recognizes CRLF as one terminator and lone CR or LF as terminators. Each terminator contributes one line; a nonempty final unterminated segment contributes one. Empty input has zero lines, trailing terminators create no phantom line, and other Unicode separators do not terminate lines. Words follow Python `str.split` Unicode whitespace semantics.

By default, remove exactly one leading U+FEFF. Preserve interior BOMs and every BOM when `strip_bom=False` or `--keep-bom` is selected. A retained BOM is ordinary non-whitespace. Files decode as strict UTF-8; API failures retain OSError subclasses or UnicodeDecodeError, produce no partial result, and close owned handles. API calls are silent and inputs remain unchanged.

## Delivery boundaries

| Phase and milestone | Intended useful outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Phase 1, milestone 1.1 | Named-file counting through the public API and `python -m textstats [--keep-bom] INPUT`; exactly one input and `--` for dash-prefixed filenames. Success returns 0 with exactly `lines=<N> words=<N>\n` on stdout and empty stderr; help returns 0. |
| Phase 1, milestone 1.2 | Failure handling, public API/module documentation, runnable README and distribution exits. Input/read/decode failures return 1; missing/extra inputs and unknown options return 2. Failures identify the problem on stderr with empty stdout and no traceback. |
| Phase 2, milestone 2.1 | `--json` emits one object plus newline, with integer `lines` and `words` fields only and identical counts. Text remains the default; JSON key order and spacing are unrestricted. |
| Phase 2, milestone 2.2 | `-` reads stdin bytes to EOF and decodes UTF-8 independently of locale without closing stdin. Empty stdin counts (0, 0); read/decode errors return 1 and identify stdin. Final exits cover documentation, distribution and retained behavior. |

Product tests must be discoverable and nonempty under `tests/unit/` and `tests/integration/`. Workflow fixture checks belong separately under `tests/workflows/`. Distribution verification must invoke the extracted source package's module entry. Exact test commands and package layout will be established during planning, rather than claimed as runnable at this stage.

## Later separately requested range feature

Retain this feature as a future design constraint and separate delivery boundary, outside the initial two-phase executable hierarchy. It will add exactly one `--lines START:END` or `--lines=START:END`, using positive ASCII decimal inclusive one-based endpoints with START <= END and decimal leading zeros. There is no arbitrary endpoint limit. Reject signs, whitespace, Unicode digits, zero, reversed endpoints, open endpoints, extra colons, missing values and repeated range options with usage status 2 before acquiring input.

Complete input must decode before selection, including bytes after END. Apply BOM policy once before line numbering, preserve selected content and terminators, and select the available subset or zero beyond EOF. Exposing an interior BOM must not strip it. Options compose in either order. Public API signatures and exports stay whole-input. Named-file text/JSON range behavior is this feature's delivery boundary; source-independent compatibility with future stdin is required, while stdin acquisition and delivery remain their own later milestone.

## Acceptance anchors

The eventual specification must retain the full supplied examples and invalid-range matrix. Key anchors are empty input (0, 0), BOM-only default (0, 0), retained BOM (1, 1), two leading BOMs under default policy (1, 1), LF-only (1, 0), `alpha\n\n` (2, 1), and `alpha` followed by U+2028 and `beta` (1, 2). These distinguish terminator counting, Unicode word splitting and exactly-once BOM removal.

For `alpha beta\nbeta\nlast two`, ranges 2:3 and 2:99 yield (2, 3), 1:1 yields (1, 2), and 4:99 yields (0, 0). Blank selected lines and mixed CRLF/CR/LF must retain their counts. No new performance targets, third-party runtime dependencies or extra CLI capabilities are inferred.

# TextStats architecture

## Scope and governing input

This document describes the intended architecture for the capabilities and staged scope in the accepted [project brief](PROJECT.md). No product implementation exists. The public surface is an importable `textstats` API and `python -m textstats`; counting has no runtime dependencies beyond Python 3.11+ and the standard library.

## Major blocks and dependency direction

| Block | Responsibility and dependencies |
| --- | --- |
| Counting core | Own immutable statistics and text semantics: BOM normalization, CRLF/CR/LF logical-line handling and Unicode whitespace word counting. It depends on Python strings and immutable results, with no filesystem, CLI or process-stream dependency. |
| Input acquisition | Own strict UTF-8 decoding and named-file handle lifetime. It supplies decoded text to the counting pipeline and propagates acquisition/decode errors. Future stdin acquisition uses bytes and retains external stream ownership. |
| Public API facade | Directly expose the three requested public exports. `count_text` invokes the text pipeline; `count_file` acquires named-file text and invokes equivalent whole-input counting. Both return statistics silently, retaining API exceptions. |
| CLI orchestration | Parse and validate the requested invocation before acquiring input, select BOM/output policies, invoke the counting pipeline and translate input failures into CLI diagnostics/status. It depends on acquisition and core contracts; neither depends on CLI. |
| Presentation | Format a completed result as the required text output or the later JSON object. The CLI owns stdout/stderr effects and process status; presentation contains no input acquisition or counting rules. |

These are logical responsibility blocks, not a requirement for separate files or classes. Detailed collaborating components belong in decomposition and physical allocation in layout. There is no dependency cycle or global mutable counting state. The API and CLI share counting and decoding semantics rather than maintaining independent algorithms.

## Text pipeline and ownership

Acquisition finishes strict decoding before a result can be computed or emitted. The text pipeline removes at most one leading BOM according to the selected policy, then operates on normalized text. Whole-input API calls never select a range. The pipeline provides a counting path for already normalized text so the later CLI range path cannot strip a newly exposed interior BOM.

A shared logical-line representation or traversal recognizes only CRLF, CR and LF and preserves terminators and content. Both counting and future selection must use this semantic boundary; Python's broader Unicode `splitlines` behavior is unsuitable. Word counting remains independent, using `str.split` semantics on the counted content. Decomposition will settle the small internal interfaces without adding public exports.

The future range pipeline is acquisition and complete decode, BOM normalization once, logical-line selection, then counting and presentation. Parsing/validation precedes acquisition. Selection does not depend on whether text originated from a file or stdin. This supports the requested compatibility constraint without implementing the range feature or moving stdin into its delivery scope.

Input acquisition owns handles it opens and closes them on success and failure. Callers retain ownership of supplied process streams, including future stdin. No block writes input content. Statistics are immutable values; transient decoded strings and selected content have invocation-local lifetime. The default architecture holds complete decoded input in memory, which simplifies strict complete-decode and no-partial-result guarantees. No bounded-memory target was requested; streaming remains a future reconsideration if a concrete input-size constraint arises.

## Failure and output boundaries

API adapters allow the required filesystem and decode exception types to reach callers and produce no output. CLI orchestration distinguishes usage failures from input/read/decode failures and maps them to the prescribed statuses. Successful acquisition and counting must complete before stdout emission; diagnostics identify the affected input, and expected user failures do not expose a traceback. Presentation receives a complete immutable result, preventing partial count output during read/decode failure.

The CLI selects text output by default; JSON is a later output policy over the same statistics. Byte acquisition for future stdin keeps strict UTF-8 decoding independent of locale. Option parsing is a CLI concern and does not alter public whole-input API signatures.

## Consequential choices and verification seams

Use plain functions and a small immutable result value. Separate pure text processing from I/O and process effects because they have different failure/lifetime rules and verification seams. A monolithic CLI would couple reusable API behavior to streams; a class hierarchy, plugin system or configurable decoding layer would introduce unsupported variation. The selected function pipeline provides the required extension seams with less state and indirection.

Unit tests can exercise immutable results, BOM policy and logical-line/word semantics directly. Integration tests can exercise named-file acquisition, subprocess CLI output/status, later JSON/stdin behavior and extracted-source module execution. Product suites remain nonempty and discoverable under the requested unit/integration directories; coordinator workflow fixtures stay separately owned. API/module documentation and README usage will expose the same contracts used by these checks.

The distribution boundary is a source package that remains importable and supports module execution after extraction. Package contents and the executable verification command are planning/layout decisions. No additional runtime dependency, installed console-script entry or network service is required.

# TextStats component decomposition

## Governing design and scope

This component model refines the accepted [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) and [project brief](PROJECT.md). Components are logical units with stable design identities; internal function names below express interface shape and may be finalized during implementation without changing their obligations. They prescribe no physical file inventory or implementation order. No production code exists.

## Components and boundaries

| ID / component | Provided boundary and owner responsibility | Required collaborators and exclusions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C-001 Statistics value | Public immutable `TextStats(lines: int, words: int)` with nonnegative counts. Own construction invariants and value representation. | No acquisition, output or normalization. SPEC will settle invalid-construction exceptions and integer-domain details. |
| C-002 BOM normalization | Internal `normalize_text(text, strip_bom) -> str`; remove exactly one leading BOM when selected and retain all other characters. Own this policy once per pipeline invocation. | Strings only; no decode, line selection or counting. |
| C-003 Logical-line traversal | Internal `logical_lines(normalized_text)` yields nonempty logical segments with their original content and CRLF/CR/LF terminators; blank terminated lines remain segments. A final nonempty unterminated segment is yielded; empty text yields none. | No BOM handling or Unicode-whitespace splitting. This is the shared line boundary for counting and future selection. |
| C-004 Normalized counting | Internal `count_normalized(normalized_text) -> TextStats`; derive line count from C-003 and word count from `str.split` on the same text. | C-001 and C-003; never normalize again, acquire input or emit output. |
| C-005 Byte acquisition and decode | Acquire complete bytes from a named file and decode strict UTF-8 without text newline translation. Own opening and closing named-file handles on every path. Future borrowed-stdin acquisition reads its binary stream to EOF and never closes it. | Python filesystem/binary stream operations; no BOM removal, range selection, counting or output. Preserve acquisition and decode exceptions for callers. |
| C-006 Public API adapters | Directly expose C-001 plus `count_text(text: str, *, strip_bom: bool = True)` and `count_file(path: str | os.PathLike[str], *, strip_bom: bool = True)`. Adapt whole-input requests to C-002/C-004; file calls use C-005 first. | No CLI invocation or range argument; no extra public export, stream output or exception-to-status translation. |
| C-007 CLI invocation parser | Validate option syntax and exactly one input; provide input identity and BOM/output policy. Future range validation supplies numeric endpoints before input acquisition. | No C-005 access during parsing. Help and usage termination belong to CLI control, not API behavior. |
| C-008 CLI controller | Coordinate parsed invocation, acquisition, text pipeline and result rendering; map expected usage/acquisition/decode failures to identifying diagnostics/status. Own process-stream writes. | C-007, C-005, C-002, C-004 and C-009; no separate counting algorithm. Future C-010 sits between normalization and counting. |
| C-009 Result rendering | Internal renderer transforms completed C-001 into the specified text string or later JSON object plus newline. | No stream write, acquisition, normalization or counting. Controller chooses format and emits result. |
| C-010 Future range selection | Future internal `select_lines(normalized_text, start, end) -> str`, with inclusive one-based endpoints, preserving available selected segments and their terminators. | C-003 and validated CLI endpoints; no input-source dependency or BOM normalization. This future feature is outside the initial two-phase executable hierarchy. |

The identities group coherent verification obligations and provide downstream specification/planning traceability; they do not require one module or task per row. No focused children are necessary for this compact component set.

## Collaboration and data lifetime

`count_text` receives the complete string, normalizes through C-002 and counts through C-004. `count_file` uses C-005 to acquire/decode complete input, then follows the equivalent public whole-input pipeline. The API adapters return C-001 without writing stdout/stderr. Strict byte decoding preserves CRLF, lone CR and LF exactly rather than relying on universal-newline text mode.

The CLI parses and validates before C-005 acquires input. C-008 then normalizes exactly once and passes normalized text to C-004. Only a completed value reaches C-009 and only the controller writes its output. If the future range feature is separately requested, C-008 passes normalized text through C-010 first and sends its result directly to C-004, bypassing C-002 a second time. Consequently, a BOM exposed inside selected content remains ordinary non-whitespace.

C-003 yields segments such as `a\r\n`, `b c\r` and `d\n` without changing characters. Selecting whole segments and concatenating them preserves line boundaries for C-004 and preserves Unicode whitespace for word counting. Segment enumeration can be lazy over the already decoded string; it does not imply streaming decode or partial input acceptance. Counting and range selection share the same terminator semantics.

For future stdin, C-005 obtains bytes from the externally owned binary input stream and returns decoded text after EOF; the remainder of the pipeline is identical. The parser/controller activate that acquisition choice only at its delivery milestone. Decoded strings, segments and results are local to an invocation; there is no shared mutable counting state or input mutation.

## Failure and verification seams

C-001 can be checked through construction, immutability and value assertions. C-002 can be checked with empty, BOM-only, repeated-leading and interior-BOM strings under both policies. C-003/C-004 can be checked with mixed terminators, consecutive blank lines, final segments and Unicode whitespace/separators. These seams need no filesystem or subprocess.

C-005 can be checked with temporary valid/invalid UTF-8 files, missing/unreadable paths and controlled read failures, including handle cleanup. Borrowed-stream checks later verify byte decoding, locale independence, EOF and retained ownership. C-006 checks establish direct imports, whole-input equivalence, silence and exception propagation. No partial decoded/count result is returned on input failure.

C-007 checks establish help/usage behavior and, later, range validation before acquisition, including repeated options and unbounded decimal endpoints. C-008/C-009 checks establish exact text output, JSON field/type constraints, empty failure stdout and identifying stderr/status. Subprocess integration validates the real module entry and extracted-source distribution; component-level seams support controlled acquisition failures that can be difficult to reproduce reliably through platform permissions.

C-010's future checks cover available subsets, beyond-EOF emptiness, blank selected lines, mixed terminators, bad bytes after END and interior BOM exposure. These are deferred feature obligations, not tests or delivery included in this preparation request.

# Shared Markdown style

Apply these rules whenever SDD Manager authors, revises or reviews Markdown. They cover all document types: main and feature development documents and focused children, active reports, README and guides, AGENTS.md, skill instructions and references, templates, release notes and hosted Markdown drafts. Direct skill calls use the same rules as coordinated workflows. Respect controlling human/project instructions; surface a real conflict rather than silently choosing an incompatible format.

## Heading separation

Place a blank line after every Markdown heading, including ATX (`#` through `######`) and Setext headings (text followed by an `=` or `-` underline). This applies before prose, another heading, a list, a table or a fenced block. Separate headings from preceding content with a blank line as well; the beginning of a document or template needs no leading blank line. A heading at the end of a file still has a following blank line.

## List separation

Place a blank line before and after each entire top-level, non-indented list. Treat its nested items and continuation blocks as part of that list. Do not require blank lines around nested lists or between ordinary list items; compact nesting is preferred when the content permits it. No leading blank line is needed when a list begins the document; a final list has a trailing blank line.

## Indentation and lists

Use spaces, never tabs, for Markdown structural indentation. Use **four spaces per indentation level**, including nested bulleted, numbered, mixed and task lists. Start a top-level list at its container's left margin; indent each child list four additional spaces relative to its parent. Keep siblings at the same indentation and preserve their intended parentage.

Use **exactly one ordinary ASCII space after each list marker**, at every nesting level: `- item`, `* item`, `+ item`, `1. item` and `1) item`. Normally this uses the next four-space level; when a wide ordered-list marker requires more space, use the smallest additional four-space level that reaches the item's content column. Do not trade valid Markdown attachment for a mechanically fixed absolute column. Place a blank line before and after code blocks, including fenced and indented blocks. Apply this separation to blocks nested in list items as well, keeping them attached to their item. # TextStats repository layout

## Governing placement and current state

This proposal allocates the accepted [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) and [components](DECOMPOSITION.md) to physical ownership supporting the accepted [PLAN strategy](PLAN.md) and [SPEC](SPEC.md). Only root orientation/bootstrap and development documents currently exist. All source, product tests, API documentation and tools below are proposed paths; this preparation creates none of their implementation files. No focused layout children are needed.

Use a flat `textstats/` package so `python -m textstats` and direct imports work from a source checkout or extracted source root without an installation dependency. This suits the standard-library-only utility. Extracted-source checks isolate the working directory and import environment rather than relying on the checkout's package.

## Source ownership

| Proposed path | Components and responsibility | Allowed dependency direction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `textstats/core.py` | C-001 statistics value, C-002 normalization, C-003 logical-line traversal, C-004 normalized counting and C-006's text adapter. Own pure semantics and `count_text`. | Standard library and strings only; no acquisition, CLI or stream output. |
| `textstats/io.py` | C-005 complete strict byte acquisition/decoding and C-006's named-file adapter `count_file`. Future borrowed-stdin byte reader lives here. | Depends on core for whole-input counting; no CLI/presentation. |
| `textstats/__init__.py` | C-006 public facade: directly re-export `TextStats`, `count_text` and `count_file`, with those names as the intended public API. | Imports core/io; no input or process effect on import. |
| `textstats/cli.py` | C-007 parser, C-008 controller and C-009 rendering as cohesive small CLI functions. | Depends on core/io; neither depends on CLI. |
| `textstats/__main__.py` | Minimal module-entry adapter invoking CLI control and returning process status. | Depends on cli only; counting/error policy remains in its owner. |

Co-locate the tightly related pure operations in core and the small parser/controller/rendering functions in cli rather than imposing one module per logical component. The separation still supports localized verifiable tasks and pure/I/O/process seams. Physical names do not create new public exports. C-010 has no implementation file in this request: a separately accepted feature can place pure selection alongside shared traversal in core or propose a focused layout amendment if justified.

## Tests and check tools

| Proposed path | Owner and verification purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/__init__.py`, `tests/unit/__init__.py`, `tests/integration/__init__.py` | Unittest package/discovery support. Empty package markers are infrastructure and do not count as product tests. |
| `tests/unit/test_core.py` | Value/constructor invariants, pure line/word/BOM and public text semantics. |
| `tests/unit/test_io.py` | Strict decode, file exception and owned-handle lifetime seams; later borrowed-stdin byte/read/ownership seams. |
| `tests/unit/test_cli.py` | Parser/controller/rendering seams and controlled read failures without platform permission assumptions. |
| `tests/integration/test_api.py` | Direct import/signature/silence and real text/file equivalence/input preservation across public adapters. |
| `tests/integration/test_cli.py` | Real module subprocess input/output/status/help/usage, named-file/BOM and later JSON/stdin behavior. |
| `tests/integration/test_distribution.py` | Extracted-source archive and module-entry acceptance through the distribution checker. |
| `tests/workflows/` | Separate workflow fixture checks if later authorized. They are excluded from product discovery and distribution. Existing coordinator fixtures stay in their protected locations. |
| `tools/check_tests.py` | Standard-library unittest runner discovering unit and integration independently, reporting actual collection counts, rejecting either zero-count suite and returning nonzero on failure. |
| `tools/package_source.py` | Standard-library source archive builder with an explicit allowlist and reusable build boundary. |
| `tools/check_distribution.py` | Build/extract into a temporary isolated directory, invoke the extracted module entry, and verify delivered behavior without importing the original checkout. |

The tools are planned delivery code, not present utilities. Temporary test inputs and failure streams are generated by tests, kept outside tracked source and cleaned up; no copied test transcript or secret goes into product fixtures. Unit and integration discovery are explicit, so workflow checks cannot substitute for meaningful product tests.

## Documentation, archives and preserved resources

| Path | Ownership/status |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md` | Existing root product entry; runnable setup/API/CLI/test/distribution usage added with delivery and updated for phase 2. |
| `docs/public-api.md` | Proposed public module/API reference covering the SPEC contracts and resource/failure behavior. Public module/function docstrings live with their source owners. |
| `docs/dev/` roots and adjacent QC reports | Existing governing preparation; TASKS becomes the canonical executable owner after acceptance, not a copied checklist elsewhere. |
| `docs/dev/reports/phases/<phase-id>/<milestone-id>.md`, `PHASE-REPORT.md` and `docs/dev/reports/IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT.md` | Planned execution evidence under the pinned lifecycle, created by the owning review tasks. |
| `dist/` | Generated source archives, excluded by existing ignore rules. Proposed archive basename is `textstats-source.zip`, with top-level `textstats-source/`. No product version is inferred. |
| `AI_DISCLOSURE.md`, `SDD-MANAGER.md`, `AGENTS.md` | Existing root disclosure/usage/orientation; maintain truthful current navigation with owning checkpoints. |
| `textstats-run-resources/`, `.github/`, `docs/testing/publisher-037/` | Existing coordinator-owned resources; preserve unchanged and exclude from product archive. |

The source archive allowlist is the product package, README, public API reference, disclosure/usage notices and the package builder/checker. Exclude development/campaign records, product test implementation unless expressly needed later, workflow fixtures, credentials, helper files, generated caches and unrelated resources. The archive contains every public module/API document required by R-013 and can run the module from its extracted source root. Packaging/checking does not require installed third-party build tools or a console-script entry.

## Planned commands and readiness limits

Run commands from the product repository root after their owning delivery tasks provide the named files. These commands are proposed and have not been validated against nonexistent product code.

| Command | Intended evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `python -m textstats INPUT` | Real named-file module entry; later flags/input follow delivered SPEC behavior. |
| `python tools/check_tests.py` | Nonzero discovery counts for unit and integration, followed by unittest execution with failure propagated. |
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests/unit -t . -v` | Focused unit suite; inspect reported count above zero. |
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests/integration -t . -v` | Focused integration suite; inspect reported count above zero. |
| `python tools/package_source.py` | Allowlisted source archive in ignored dist output. |
| `python tools/check_distribution.py` | Extracted-source named-file/text/failure and delivered JSON/stdin module-entry acceptance. |

Distribution checking uses a temporary extraction root as subprocess cwd, sanitizes checkout import paths such as PYTHONPATH and verifies the imported `textstats` location belongs to the extracted root. Its actual acceptance invocation is `python -m textstats` from that source root; an archive listing or import smoke alone cannot satisfy R-013. Test/check subprocesses use the same selected Python executable so installed-package assumptions cannot mask missing source files.

Python 3.12.14 is available in the current preparation environment; delivery supports Python 3.11+. Existing ignore rules remain preserved. If generated Python caches require additional ignore entries during implementation, add narrowly scoped rules with the owning task instead of changing coordinator resources or broad cleanup.

## Layout assessment checkpoint

The adjacent [PLAN review report](PLAN-REVIEW-REPORT.md) covers combined strategy/placement readiness. Ownership maps every current component and required test/document/distribution boundary without cycles or ambiguous source allocation. Source-independent range/stdin design remains intact. No unresolved placement choice blocks later task derivation.

The coordinator accepted this layout and combined PLAN QC at commit `b3ba0338d71c167aaec8ca85317d09002557ea2d`, layout blob `4039da9d2e0422ad3b53fc82f18b63612e75ccac` and report blob `b59fa054824a3a8768e59c2dc15f90c7b9b7d330`, under delegated test-artifact review authority; published decision evidence is `0e5c6d9`. Full assessment found no material placement issue. This scoped decision enables TASKS/owner QC, without authorizing implementation or preaccepting unseen tasks.
